title: Benchmark run capacity window plan (multi-region) — Latency/$ public report
author: Sean Gallagher
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the capacity windows, safety limits, monitoring, and rollback criteria for executing the Latency/$ benchmark suite across regions without impacting production SLOs.

This is the SRE-owned plan used by Perf/Evals and the benchmark-lab operator during scheduled runs.

## Scope
**In scope**
- Reserved benchmark windows by region for the public Latency/$ benchmark suite (chat + embeddings workloads)
- Resource isolation and throttles (rate limits, concurrency caps, autoscaling constraints)
- Monitoring requirements and “stop conditions”
- Rollback plan if production risk appears

**Out of scope**
- Methodology details (prompts, exact distributions, scoring); see methodology page
- Claim language; see public benchmarking claims guidelines

## Roles & on-call expectations
**Primary owners**
- SRE run owner (per window): **Sean Gallagher** (backup: **Vanessa Ortiz**)
- Capacity guardrails sponsor: **Neha Kapoor**
- Benchmark operator: **Rina Kobayashi**
- Perf/Evals sign-off: **Claire Dubois**

**During each window**
- SRE run owner is in the war-room and is the final decision maker on pause/stop.
- Benchmark operator runs benchmark-lab and follows the throttles in this plan.
- If a stop condition is triggered: operator halts runs immediately; SRE owner decides rollback/escalation.

## Regions covered
Benchmarks will be executed in the same regions used in the public report. Region names below reflect Redwood routing regions and their primary cloud footprint.

- **NA:** us-east (IAD), us-west (PDX)
- **EU:** eu-central (FRA), eu-west (DUB)
- **APAC:** ap-southeast (SIN)

If additional regions are added to the report, this plan must be updated and re-approved by SRE + Perf/Evals.

## Capacity strategy (high level)
1) **Use dedicated benchmark capacity where available.** If a region has a benchmark-only GPU pool, runs must be pinned to it.
2) **If shared fleet is required**, enforce strict request throttles and pool saturation caps.
3) **Prefer off-peak** local time for each region.
4) **Short, repeatable slices** over long continuous runs: multiple 30–60 minute runs with validation between slices reduces blast radius.

## Reserved benchmark windows (initial run + rerun buffer)
All times are local to the region unless noted.

### Window schedule table
| Region | Primary window | Rerun buffer | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| us-east (IAD) | Tue/Thu 19:00–22:00 ET | Fri 19:00–21:00 ET | Avoid known weekly batch jobs (Wed). |
| us-west (PDX) | Mon/Wed 19:00–22:00 PT | Thu 19:00–21:00 PT | Coordinate with USW capacity rebalancing. |
| eu-central (FRA) | Tue/Thu 20:00–23:00 CET | Fri 20:00–22:00 CET | EU data residency messaging depends on stable EU results. |
| eu-west (DUB) | Mon/Wed 20:00–23:00 GMT | Thu 20:00–22:00 GMT | Keep separate from FRA to reduce cross-EU contention. |
| ap-southeast (SIN) | Tue/Thu 20:00–23:00 SGT | Sat 10:00–12:00 SGT | Weekend buffer reduces contention with APAC peak. |

### Change control
- Any shift of >2 hours or any additional “ad hoc” window requires SRE run owner approval in #eng-sre and update of the launch checklist.

## Safety limits (hard caps)
These caps apply regardless of the benchmark configuration and are intended to prevent production impact.

### Fleet utilization caps
**Stop using shared fleet** if any of these are true:
- Region aggregate GPU utilization (serving pools) sustains **>85% for 10 minutes**
- Region queue time / admission delay sustains **>2s p95 for 5 minutes**
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) exceeds **0.5% for 5 minutes** on production traffic

### Benchmark traffic caps (per region)
Benchmark operator must enforce these controls in benchmark-lab.

- **Max benchmark share of region tokens:** target <= **10%** of typical off-peak token volume; hard cap **15%**
- **Max benchmark concurrency:** hard cap **25 concurrent requests** per model variant (chat) and **50 concurrent requests** per embedding model
- **Max request rate:** hard cap **40 RPS** (chat) and **80 RPS** (embeddings) per region
- **Max output tokens:** hard cap **1,024 output tokens** per request for chat runs
- **KV/prefix cache policy:** benchmark runs must use the approved methodology setting; do not enable experimental caching modes during public runs

### Autoscaling constraints
- Do not change region autoscaling policies to “make benchmarks look better.”
- Allowed temporary changes during a window are limited to **benchmark pool** min/max replicas only.
- Any change to production pool min/max replicas requires SRE lead approval and must be reverted immediately after the window.

## Pre-flight checklist (T-60 to T-10 minutes)
SRE run owner completes:
1) Confirm region health is green (no active incidents, no degraded dependencies).
2) Verify capacity headroom:
   - GPUs available >= **N+2** per target model pool (where N is planned benchmark allocation)
   - No scheduled maintenance in cloud region during the window
3) Confirm guardrails are armed:
   - Alerts enabled for GPU utilization, queue time, p95 latency, and 5xx/timeout rates
   - Canary gating policy active (see perf-canary guardrails page)
4) Confirm benchmark operator has:
   - Correct region pinning
   - Correct model/version pins for the report
   - Throttles set to this plan’s caps
5) Announce start in war-room channel with a single message template (see “Comms” section).

## Monitoring requirements (dashboards + key graphs)
During the run, SRE run owner must keep these panels visible for the active region:

**Region health & capacity**
- GPU utilization by pool (p50/p95 over 5m)
- GPU memory pressure / OOM counts
- Request admission / queue time (p50/p95)
- Autoscaler actions (scale up/down events)

**Serving quality**
- Production latency p50/p95 for top 3 routes in region
- 5xx + timeout rate (production vs benchmark separated if possible)
- Saturation indicators: active batches, batch queue depth, scheduler lag

**Cost/metering sanity**
- Token accounting anomalies (sudden drops/spikes)
- Cost attribution pipeline lag (ensure metric freshness is within expected bounds)

**Required artifacting**
- Capture at least one screenshot set per region per window:
  - Start-of-window baseline (5 minutes)
  - Mid-window (peak benchmark load)
  - End-of-window (cooldown)
- Save to the benchmarking screenshots index.

## Stop conditions (immediate pause/terminate)
If any stop condition triggers, the benchmark operator must halt new load within 60 seconds (stop sending requests), and SRE run owner decides whether to resume.

### Production SLO risk triggers
Immediate stop if any of the following occur and persist beyond the grace period:
- Production p95 latency for top routes in region regresses by **>15% for 10 minutes**
- Production error rate (5xx + timeouts) exceeds **0.5% for 5 minutes**
- Admission delay / queue time p95 exceeds **2s for 5 minutes**
- Any paging incident is declared in the region (regardless of presumed cause)

### Infrastructure instability triggers
Immediate stop if:
- OOM rate increases materially (more than **3 OOMs in 10 minutes** in a model pool used by production)
- Autoscaler thrash (>= **6 scale events in 15 minutes**) in a production pool
- Notable dependency degradation (KV store, routing control plane, auth) correlated with benchmark load

## Rollback plan
Rollback actions are ordered from least invasive to most invasive.

### Level 0: Pause benchmark load (default first action)
- Stop benchmark-lab traffic immediately.
- Maintain observation for 10 minutes to confirm recovery.
- If recovery occurs, resume at **50% of prior load** and reassess after 15 minutes.

### Level 1: Reduce benchmark allocation / isolate traffic
- Re-pin benchmarks to benchmark-only pool if available.
- Reduce concurrency caps by 50%.
- Reduce max output tokens (chat) to 512 if methodology permits (if not permitted, do not change; rerun later).

### Level 2: Revert temporary scaling changes (if any)
- Revert any benchmark pool min/max replica changes.
- Confirm autoscaler policy is back to baseline.

### Level 3: Production protection
- Trigger canary gating to shed benchmark traffic entirely.
- If needed, enforce stricter region-wide rate limits on the benchmark API key(s).

### Level 4: Incident response
- Declare incident if production impact continues >10 minutes after Level 0.
- Engage on-call for serving runtime and infra as needed.

## Post-window steps (T+0 to T+30 minutes)
1) Confirm region has returned to baseline:
   - GPU utilization normal
   - Production p95 latency normal
   - Error rate normal
2) Benchmark operator uploads run artifacts (results + config hash) to the benchmark artifacts store.
3) SRE run owner notes any anomalies:
   - Whether stop conditions triggered
   - Any suspected noise sources (neighbor workload, autoscaler, dependency)
4) If rerun needed, schedule within the region’s rerun buffer window and link to anomaly triage playbook.

## Comms plan
**War-room channel:** #eng-sre-benchmark-windows (secondary: #eng-sre)

### Start-of-window message template
- Region:
- Window:
- Operator:
- Models/versions pinned:
- Benchmark caps (concurrency/RPS):
- Dashboards link:
- Stop condition reminder: SRE has final stop/resume authority

### Stop event message template
- STOP triggered at (time):
- Region:
- Trigger metric + threshold:
- Action taken (pause/load reduction/rollback level):
- Next update ETA:

## Approvals
This plan is approved for execution when:
- SRE run owner + capacity sponsor approve (Sean Gallagher / Neha Kapoor)
- Perf/Evals approve that the safety limits do not invalidate methodology (Claire Dubois)

## Notes & rationale (why these numbers)
- The 10–15% benchmark token share is chosen to keep headroom for natural traffic bursts and avoid confounding results due to queueing artifacts.
- The latency regression trigger (>15% for 10 minutes) is designed to catch sustained customer impact while avoiding false positives from short-lived noise.
- Short repeated windows reduce the chance that a single noisy period dominates results and make it easier to isolate infra anomalies.

## Appendix: Known high-risk periods (avoid scheduling)
- End-of-month (billing and reporting jobs): last business day 17:00–21:00 local
- Major product launches / press events: coordinate with Marketing calendar
- Large fleet maintenance windows: see SRE weekly maintenance bulletin
